query.question: How has Acme Cloud's strategy changed over the last 90 days?

insight.summary: Over the past 90 days, Acme Cloud has strategically pivoted toward an AI-first analytics positioning while systematically building out enterprise readiness. Concurrently, the company adjusted its commercial model by lowering entry-tier pricing and gating advanced AI capabilities behind higher-tier enterprise and usage-based packages.
observed_changes: Pivoted product focus and marketing messaging toward AI-first analytics and automated time-to-insight, rolling out an AI assistant, anomaly detection, and AI-generated executive reports.
Strengthened enterprise governance and GTM capacity by adding SSO, advanced access controls, and audit logs alongside hiring for enterprise account executives and enterprise customer success roles.

Bifurcated pricing and packaging by reducing the Pro plan price from $49 to $39 per month, introducing high-volume usage-based pricing, and bundling advanced AI analytics into higher-tier enterprise plans.
Expanded integration capabilities by introducing native CRM connectors and connections to external business data sources.
insight.strategic_signal: This coordinated pattern could suggest a barbell go-to-market strategy: reducing entry-level friction to drive top-of-funnel user adoption while monetizing high-value accounts through enterprise-grade security controls, dedicated sales support, and premium AI packaging.
watch_next: Further gating or tiering of core versus advanced AI features across subscription plans.
Additional enterprise compliance announcements, SLAs, or dedicated deployment options.
Subsequent pricing or packaging adjustments for data connectors and usage consumption tiers.

Introduced a native CRM data connector
Introduced an enterprise security package with advanced access controls
